'''''Nolina''''' is a [[genus]] of temperate and tropical [[xerophytic]] [[flowering plant]]s belonging to the family [[Asparagaceae]]. The native distribution of the genus includes most of [[Mexico]] and the southern regions of the [[United States]] north to [[Nevada]] and [[Colorado]].<ref name="POWO" /><ref name="eFloras">{{cite web |last=Hess |first=William J. |title='''Nolina''' Michaux, Fl. Bor.-Amer. 1: 207. 1803. |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=122374 |access-date=2011-08-06 |work=Flora of North America |publisher=eFloras.org}}</ref><ref name=":7">Hochstätter, F. (2010). The genus ''Nolina'' (Nolinaceae). Piante Grasse 2010(1, Suppl.): 1-48.</ref><ref>[http://bonap.net/NAPA/TaxonMaps/Genus/County/Nolina Biota of North America Program, 2013 county distribution maps]</ref><ref>Trelease, William. 1911.  Proceedings of the American Philosophical Society 50(200)</ref> Especially in the USA, members of the genus are known as '''beargrass''',<ref name="ITIS">{{ITIS |id=42983 |taxon=''Nolina'' |accessdate=2011-08-06}}</ref> some of which are cultivated as [[ornamental plant]]s.

''Nolina'' species grow large rosettes of many leaves, with many species forming large, erect trunks, with some species branching to contain multiple rosettes of leaves, while others are stemless. They are typically large plants, and are [[dioecious]], with male and female flowers being produced on different plants.<ref name="eFloras" /><ref name=":7" /><ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1600/036364418X697436 |title=The Genus ''Nolina'' (Asparagaceae) of the Baja California Peninsula, and the Recognition of a New Species Combination |year=2018 |last1=Hernández-Sandoval |first1=Luis |last2=Rebman |first2=Jon P. |journal=Systematic Botany |volume=43 |issue=3 |pages=717–733 |s2cid=91615592}}</ref>

The genus was named by [[André Michaux]] after the 18th century French arboriculturist Abbé C. P. Nolin.<ref name="eFloras" /> The [[type species]] is ''[[Nolina georgiana]]'', the only species included by Michaux in the new genus he described;<ref name="Michaux">{{cite book | last=Michaux | first=André | title=Flora Boreali-Americana, sistens caracteres plantarum quas in America septentrionali collegit et detexit Andreas Michaux | publisher=Levrault | publication-place=Parisiis et Argentorati | year=1803 | doi=10.5962/bhl.title.5088 | doi-access=free | url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/itempdf/24879 | access-date=2025-08-13 | pages=207–208}}</ref> this is one of the stemless species, without any trunk.<ref name="FNAgeorgiana">{{cite web | title=''Nolina georgiana'' in Flora of North America @ efloras.org | website=eFloras.org Home | url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=220009266 | access-date=2025-08-13}}</ref>

== Classification ==
In the [[APG III system|APG III classification system]] of [[plant taxonomy]], ''Nolina'' is a member of the family [[Asparagaceae]], and within this family, ''Nolina'' is part of a subfamily, the [[Convallarioideae]]. In the past, many members of the Convallarioideae, including ''Nolina'', were placed in the now defunct family Ruscaceae).<ref>{{Citation |last1=Chase |first1=M.W. |last2=Reveal |first2=J.L. |last3=Fay |first3=M.F. |year=2009 |title=A subfamilial classification for the expanded asparagalean families Amaryllidaceae, Asparagaceae and Xanthorrhoeaceae |journal=Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society |volume=161 |issue=2 |pages=132–136 |doi=10.1111/j.1095-8339.2009.00999.x|name-list-style=amp |doi-access=free }}</ref> Former alternative placements include Nolinaceae and Agavaceae.<ref name="eFloras" />

Previously, some botanists have included the genus ''[[Beaucarnea]]'' in ''Nolina'', and over time, multiple species of both genera have been moved back and forth between the two genera. More recent [[Molecular phylogenetics|molecular phylogenetic]] research found that ''Beaucarnea'' and ''Nolina'' are well supported by DNA and morphological evidence as being two distinct genera.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Rojas-Piña |first1=Vanessa |last2=Olson |first2=Mark E. |last3=Alvarado-Cárdenas |first3=Leonardo O. |last4=Eguiarte |first4=Luis E. |date=2014 |title=Molecular phylogenetics and morphology of ''Beaucarnea'' (Ruscaceae) as distinct from ''Nolina'', and the submersion of ''Calibanus'' into ''Beaucarnea'' |url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.12705/636.31 |journal=Taxon |language=en |volume=63 |issue=6 |pages=1193–1211 |doi=10.12705/636.31 |issn=1996-8175|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Description ==
''Nolina'' are perennial plants, with some growing as tufts of leaves arising from near ground level with little or only a short above ground stem, whilst others grow in a tree-like manner forming a woody, leafless caudex or trunk of up to about 2-7m, that with age, may branch to form multiple branches. The shorter species, especially those not forming an above ground stem, usually form colonies, often with many rosettes. The leaves are arranged into rosettes of many long, linear leaves, with the leaves being broader where they meet the stem.<ref name=":8">{{Cite web |title=''Nolina'' in Flora of North America @ efloras.org |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=122374 |access-date=2024-11-27 |website=www.efloras.org}}</ref>

The inflorescence consists of a scape (or a bare stem arising from the leaf rosettes) of between 5-250cm length, with panicles of flowers, of 30 to 180cm in length, held along the scape. Each node holds 2-5 functionally unisexual flowers. The tepals are white, cream or light tan. The fruits are capsular, 3-locular, 3-lobed and often inflated.<ref name=":8" />
